title: Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi Wins Best Debut Director Award at the 57th IFFI for Hanuman Ansh
subtitle: Film’s portrayal of Neem Karoli Baba’s spiritual journey receives jury recognition for bringing together culture, faith and music through simple storytelling
body_text:
Posted On: 28 NOV 2026 7:45PM by PIB Mumbai Release ID: 2343194 Views: 139 A A Print Share X Facebook Instagram WhatsApp Copy Article Link
Read in: English Marathi Malayalam हिन्दी Gujarati
Goa, 28 November 2026 Celebrating the power of content-driven cinema and compelling storytelling, Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi has won the Best Debut Director of an Indian Feature Film Award at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) for his debut feature, Hanuman Ansh . The award was presented at the festival’s closing ceremony in Goa on November 28, 2026, and carries a trophy and a cash prize of ₹5 lakh. A writer and director with over 100 projects across films, advertisements and music videos, Chaturvedi brings a diverse creative background to the film. An MBBS graduate, he practiced medicine for nearly five years before pursuing filmmaking. He has worked as a creative director, collaborated with filmmaker Anubhav Sinha and written for the television series Fauji 2 . His engagement with the life and teachings of Neem Karoli Baba also inspired his 2020 book, Divine Detour: That Changed My Life . The film’s emphasis on simplicity and emotional storytelling is reflected in the jury’s appreciation. While announcing the award, the jury highlighted that “budgets don't matter, content does” and commended Chaturvedi for bringing together culture, faith and music with a strong emotional connect. It also praised the film’s uncomplicated storytelling, describing it as a refreshing approach in an era dominated by special effects and technology. The jury further acknowledged the applause the film had received from audiences in cinema halls across the world. The Jury's citation reads: " Budgets don't matter, content does. We felicitate Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi for encapsulating this basic foundation of cinema in his debut film Hanuman Ansh." "It is an incredible feat you have achieved in bringing together culture, faith and music, tied with a strong emotional connect. In an era of special effects and technology, the simplicity in storytelling is worthy of the thunderous applause it has received in cinema halls all over the world. Our congratulations to Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi for winning the Best Debut Director for Hanuman Ansh." , the citation adds. About the film: Hanuman Ansh follows the spiritual journey of Lakshminarayan, born in a village in present-day Uttar Pradesh, as he travels across North India seeking answers to questions about life, death and human suffering. His encounters with saints and ordinary people gradually shape his understanding of spirituality, while a mysterious encounter near Neem Karoli village leads to the name Neem Karoli Baba. The film traces his transformation into a revered spiritual figure whose teachings later inspired people across the world, including Steve Jobs, Mark Zuckerberg and Julia Roberts. The first instalment of a planned trilogy, the film explores themes of simplicity, self-discovery and introspection, reminding audiences that understanding the world begins with understanding oneself. #IFFI2026 #57IFFI @IFFIGoa @MIB_India — PIB India (@PIB_India) November 28, 2026 ‘Hanuman Ansh’ Explores the Spiritual Journey of Neem Karoli Baba, Inviting Audiences to Look Within 📽️✨

▪️What if the answers to life’s most complex questions lie in the simplest of things around us? Exploring this thought through the spiritual journey of Neem Karoli Baba, Hanuman Ansh, featured in the Indian Panorama section of the 57th International Film Festival of India (#IFFI) 2026, invites audiences to pause, reflect and look within.

▪️Addressing a press conference organised by the PIB, Director Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi spoke about the inspiration behind the film and the creative philosophy that shaped its making. Crediting his mother for encouraging him to explore and learn more, he described the film as an invitation to look inward.
